title: promote-latest: a RESUMED run can move latest backwards; nothing compares a current latest with --version on resume (pair with quest-cli)
description: Found by the LCLI-631 reviewer (opum-workflow:reviewer on opum-ai/lore-cli#362, head 3439209b, 2026-09-28). This was not introduced by LCLI-631; it is the gap that task's fresh-only gate leaves open. planPromotion's gate (scripts/promote-latest.mjs, if (!resuming)) runs only on a fresh run. On a resume, main() step 4 calls validateRecord(record, {version}) on the reused record. That compares the record's own prior values with --version and never compares any package's CURRENT latest with --version. The reviewer's probe: a record for 5.6.7 with prior 5.6.6, every package's current latest at 5.7.0, and quest's latest at 5.6.7. --promote exits 0, makes six dist-tag moves to 5.6.7, and publishes the launcher with --tag latest. That is a full backwards move. Likelihood is low: step 6 requires quest's latest to equal --version, so quest must also have been moved back, by a quest rollback or the same gap on quest's side. quest-cli's promote-release.mjs has the same fresh-only behaviour: the LCLI-631/QCLI-402 verdict grid included resuming=true inputs and matched with 0 differences. So closing this is a PAIRED change, and lore must not diverge alone. Suggested rule: on resume, refuse when any package's current latest is strictly newer than --version; a package that already reads --version stays accepted, since that is what resume is for. Also from the same review: on a fresh run, a current latest that is not plain X.Y.Z is refused with validateRecord's wording 'recorded prior latest ...', although nothing has been recorded yet and the message gives no remedy. Improve that wording in the same change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The rule is agreed with quest-cli, and both sides refuse on resume when any package current latest is strictly newer than --version, before any registry write, naming both versions; a package already at --version stays accepted on resume
A verdict match by ref over fresh and resume inputs shows 0 differences between lore and quest at both final heads, with a positive control

The LCLI-631 test pinning the gap (the gate is fresh-only: resuming, an older version is accepted) is inverted to assert the refusal, and an end-to-end --promote resume test shows exit 1, zero writes, record unchanged
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

implementationNotes: PAIRED (2026-09-28). quest-cli filed the twin as QCLI-405, after reproducing the resume gap in quest's planPromotion: version 5.6.7 with every latest at 5.7.0 is refused fresh (14 problems) and accepted on resume. It adopted lore's suggested rule: on resume, refuse when any current latest is strictly newer than --version, and keep accepting a package already at --version. QCLI-405's fourth criterion is lore's verdict match on a resume grid at both final heads. quest-cli has it queued behind QCLI-331 and QCLI-330; send lore's LCLI-638 head when one exists. Separately, quest-cli's independent grid for LCLI-631/QCLI-402 (720 inputs, each side using its own RELEASE_PACKAGES) showed 0 differences; its positive control against 22a7916 showed 195.

IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-29, parent session), head 2b97082c on fix/LCLI-638-resume-refuses-newer-latest, PR opum-ai/lore-cli#392 (draft). planPromotion's package loop now compares each package's LIVE latest with --version on the resume path and refuses a strictly newer one, naming the package and both versions, before any write (the from-scratch record write is step 8; the plan is step 4). Equal-to-version and below stay accepted. Guarded on a plain X.Y.Z current, so a non-plain live latest behaves as before on resume -- deliberately out of this rule's scope. The fresh-run non-plain-current-latest refusal is re-worded into registry terms (validateRecord's 'recorded prior latest ...' named a value nothing had recorded yet) with the verdict unchanged, as the description asks. Tests in test/lcli631-promote-refuses-older-or-prerelease.test.ts (the gap test inverted per AC3, plus 8 e2e cases: exit 1, zero writes, record byte-identical, only the offending package named; accept side covers the partial move). Mutation proof with the pre-change script stashed: 6 of 8 new cases red, the 2 acceptance cases green, inverted LCLI-631 case red alone. Gates at 2b97082c: bun test 4678 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, typecheck 0, lint 0 (4 pre-existing warnings), bun run lore check 82 files 0 errors; bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0, quest 0.11.0. Runbook staging item 4 corrected ('A resumed run does not re-read a current latest against X' was true, is now false) and a CHANGELOG bullet added. AC2 (verdict match at both final heads) waits on quest-cli's QCLI-405, which is To Do; lore's head goes to them with the grid inputs. AC4's reviewer pass is running at review time; findings will be folded before the PR leaves draft.

AC2 EVIDENCE, FIRST PASS (2026-09-29, cross-session with quest-cli): the 40-row pairing grid (resuming true/false x newer/equal/older/not-plain x uniform/platform0/platform2/launcher/first4, ordinals over each side's own RELEASE_PACKAGES, VERSION 5.6.7, launcher 5.6.7-rc.N) gives IDENTICAL verdicts row for row at lore 2b97082c and quest's QCLI-405 head: 20 of 40 accepted on both sides (resume newer refused; resume equal/older/not-plain accepted; fresh equal/newer/not-plain refused; fresh older accepted). Positive control on both sides: the pre-fix scripts accept 25 of 40 and the 5 differences are exactly the resume-*-newer rows. quest-cli confirmed the two mirrors explicitly (non-plain accepted on resume; fresh-run non-plain gets the registry-terms headline), and pinned the grid durably in their test/qcli405-resume-refuses-newer-latest.test.ts. AC2 stays OPEN until both sides re-run at their FINAL heads (lore's post-review head, quest's PR head); quest-cli will send their column for the final diff.

REVIEWER F1 FIXED, head 7c193ca3 (supersedes 2b97082c). The AC4 reviewer pass measured the limit the first commit disclosed and showed it is a live instance of this task's own defect: a package whose live latest is 5.7.0-rc.1 was ACCEPTED on a 5.6.7 resume and the run then did the whole backwards move (exit 0, seven registry writes, end to end). A prerelease is strictly newer than an older release under semver precedence, so 'strictly newer' was never a plain-X.Y.Z question. Fix: leadingReleaseVersion(value) returns the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH a semver-shaped value leads with, and the resume refusal compares THAT with --version using the existing compareReleaseVersions -- precedence is decided by the release first and only a tie reaches the suffix, where it can never be higher, so no new comparator. 5.7.0-rc.1 and 5.7.0+build.7 now refuse; 5.6.7-rc.1 and 5.6.7+build.7 still resume; a value leading with no release stays unorderable and unchanged. Also fixed from the same review: the refusal no longer offers the restore-the-tag remedy (measured: --rollback refuses in exactly that state, and the manual route is the one write here with no pinned registry flags); the CHANGELOG's stale 'A resumed run is not re-checked against a current latest' sentence corrected in place; 'rather than validateRecord's ...' became 'before' (the headline is added, not a replacement); runbook and CHANGELOG now state the precedence rule. The reviewer's finding 5 (zero-byte record treated as no record, then uncaught EEXIST) is filed as LCLI-641, pre-existing and not fixed here. Grid: 70 rows, 25 accepted; pre-fix control 40 accepted with the 15 differences exactly the resume newer/prerelease-newer/build-newer rows. Gates: bun test 4685 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, typecheck 0, lore check 82 files 0 errors. The rule change has been sent to quest-cli for QCLI-405 (their grid rows for non-plain must flip from ACCEPT to REFUSE for prerelease-newer/build-newer and stay ACCEPT for prerelease-same/build-same); the reviewer is re-verifying the delta.

AC2 MATCHED AT BOTH FINAL HEADS (2026-09-29, cross-session with quest-cli; AC2's evidence, task still open only until the lore side lands). lore head 1d148358 (PR opum-ai/lore-cli#392) vs quest head 68bebc83 (squash of opum-ai/quest-cli#397, on quest dev): the 70-row grid is IDENTICAL cell for cell, 25 of 70 accepted on both sides, with matching controls. quest-cli verified the blob independently rather than taking my head claim: scripts/promote-latest.mjs is blob 9f020305e60820d9777f5894a2f67e58cf5fe0c8 at BOTH 7c193ca3 and 1d148358 (the only delta between them is a test file), and re-ran their column against 1d148358 itself. Both grids are now pinned durably as tests -- their test/qcli405-resume-refuses-newer-latest.test.ts and lore's test/lcli638-resume-refuses-newer-latest.test.ts (70 rows, asserts 25 accepted, plus the leading-release boundary and past-2^53 cases) -- with matching mutation controls: pre-fix accepts 40 of 70 and the 15 differences are exactly the resume newer/prerelease-newer/build-newer rows in all five shapes (lore 15 of 71 red when the pre-fix script is imported in place; quest the same 15 after re-pinning their control to the pre-fix blob, because their control had read origin/dev and stopped being a control the moment their fix merged -- the same shelf-life hazard lore's control avoids by being a pinned copy of f484987b:scripts/promote-latest.mjs). Both sides also measured the SAME residual and agree it is not a divergence: a NON-PLAIN --version passed directly to planPromotion with resuming:true skips the clause (RELEASE_VERSION/STRICT_SEMVER guard), identical to pre-change behaviour and unreachable through either CLI, since both refuse a non-plain --version at the artifact gate.
finalSummary:
LCLI-638, paired with quest-cli QCLI-405: planPromotion now refuses a RESUMED promotion when any package's CURRENT npm `latest` is strictly newer than --version, before any write, naming the package and both versions. The LCLI-631 gate ran on a FRESH record only, and a resume reuses the record the first run wrote, so nothing compared the registry as it reads NOW with --version: a registry that moved ahead in between made the resume move `latest` backwards, the move opum-doc's ADR refuses.

The comparison is by SEMVER PRECEDENCE, not plain-X.Y.Z equality: leadingReleaseVersion(value) returns the release a live `latest` leads with, and the existing compareReleaseVersions compares THAT with --version, so 5.7.0-rc.1 and 5.7.0+build.7 refuse while 5.6.7-rc.1 and 5.6.7+build.7 are not newer and still resume. Equal-to-version stays accepted (the partial state a resume exists for); anything below resumes normally.

VERIFIED. Pairing: the 70-row grid (resuming true/false x newer/equal/older/prerelease-newer/prerelease-same/build-newer/build-same x uniform/platform0/platform2/launcher/first4) is identical cell for cell with quest-cli's column at both final heads (lore 1d148358, quest 68bebc83), 25 of 70 accepted; quest-cli verified the script blob (9f020305) rather than my head claim, and both grids are pinned durably as tests with matching mutation controls -- pre-fix accepts 40 of 70 and the 15 differences are exactly the resume newer/prerelease-newer/build-newer rows (lore: 15 of 71 red with the pre-fix script imported in place, pinned to f484987b:scripts/promote-latest.mjs). End to end: a resume over an all-newer registry exits 1, zero registry writes, record byte-identical, stopping before the pair receipt; the accept side (partial move, uniform one-patch-below, same-release prerelease/build values, past-2^53 equal/older) still promotes. Review: an adversarial opum-workflow:reviewer pass found that my first cut's plain-X.Y.Z guard silently skipped a newer PRERELEASE -- a live instance of this task's own defect, measured end to end as a full backwards move, exit 0 with seven writes -- plus an unsupported remedy and two prose claims the change made false; all fixed at 7c193ca3 and re-verified with an independent semver spec oracle (410 curated + 28,624 randomised pairs, 7,260 near-ties, 0 disagreements), a 50,000-sample regex-completeness check, and localised mutation subsets in both directions. Gates at 1d148358: bun test 4768 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, bun run typecheck 0, bun run lint 0, bun run lore check from source 82 files 0 errors; bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0, quest 0.11.0.

ALSO IN THE SAME CHANGE: the fresh-run refusal for a package whose current `latest` is not a plain X.Y.Z now leads with a headline in the registry's own terms (before validateRecord's "recorded prior latest ...", which named a value nothing had recorded yet); the refusal no longer offers a restore-the-tag remedy that --rollback cannot perform; and the two prose claims the change made false -- the runbook's staging item and the CHANGELOG's LCLI-631 bullet, both of which said a resume is not re-checked -- are corrected in place, with a new CHANGELOG bullet.

OUT OF SCOPE, FILED: LCLI-641 (the reviewer's finding that a zero-byte promotion record is treated as no record and then dies with an uncaught EEXIST) is pre-existing, untouched here, and fails closed.
